Abstract:

Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is an emerging framework for beyond-fifth-generation and sixth-generation wireless networks in which communication and sensing share spectrum, hardware, and signalprocessing resources. Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) can control propagation by adjusting the phase of reflected signals, while rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) provides flexible multiuser interference management through common and private data streams. This research investigates RIS-assisted ISAC through optimization-based design, analytical performance evaluation, and model-driven learning.
The work completed covers baseline joint transmit beamforming and RIS reflection, robust design under imperfect channel state information (CSI), active RIS-assisted ISAC, RSMA-based ISAC beamforming, joint
RIS and RSMA optimization, analytical outage-performance evaluation, and model-driven deep learning for RIS phase optimization. Depending on the study, the metrics include communication SINR and sumrate,
radar SNR, outage probability, sensing rate, and related performance indicators. The analytical work derives outage expressions for downlink RSMA-based RIS-assisted ISAC and validates them using Monte Carlo
simulations. The learning-based work explores a model-driven neural approach for RIS phase optimization. The work done collectively address progression from baseline optimization to robustness, active surfaces,
RSMA integration, analytical evaluation, and learning-assisted design and maps these outcomes to research objectives.
